The investigation revealed that the system for the Bronglais Hospital contacting the GP was poor. The result of the DVT scan which took place on 6 February was sent to the incorrect GP surgery and despite an investigation as to why that happened no satisfactory explanation could be found. The system within the GP surgery for prescribing Rivaroxaban was poor and relied solely on receiving the notification of the results of the scan from the hospital. There was no facility to review the medication
inadequate DVT scan result communication to GP

The evidence revealed a view from one of the hospital doctors to the effect that DVT management should be undertaken within the hospital setting rather than by the GP's to ensure that a comprehensive and failsafe system operated rather than the somewhat haphazard one revealed by the evidence
inadequate DVT management coordination between hospital and GP

Overall the evidence revealed a very fragile system of communication between GP hospital and care home in circumstances in which the deceased had moved between three care homes in a short period of time
fragile communication across GP, hospital, and care home for patient moving between care homes

The system within the GP surgery for prescribing Rivaroxaban was poor and relied solely on receiving the notification of the results of the scan from the hospital. There was no facility to review the medication to ensure that the correct dosage for the correct period of time continued to be prescribed
inadequate GP medication review after DVT diagnosis
The evidence further revealed a practice of sending details of the medication and clinical plan back with the driver of the patient who had taken the patient back from hospital to the care home
inappropriate medication and plan transfer via patient transport
